title: John Lewis Student Center

name: Kyle Richardson
text: I miss Subway, Auntie Anne's, and the stained glass window, but we now have the Test Kitchen, which is always great. We have a nice ice cream place. There's even a photobooth you can use for headsets. I do wonder if the virtual clinic wasn't being used enough as that was a nice option for faculty and staff that can't use the Stamps clinic. Overall, it does seem strange that the building got bigger but we lost cool unique features. I also wish we had a computer gaming area like KSU, but I believe the console gaming service wasn't being used much. I guess much of what got lost was sort of "use it or lose it" situation ... except for Subway, but that could have been franchising headaches.
title: John Lewis Student Center

name: Subhajit Bag
text: The John Lewis Student Center at Georgia Tech is one of the best places on campus for both students and visitors. The building is modern, spacious, and full of natural light, making it a comfortable spot to hang out, study, or grab food. The variety of dining options is a big plus—you can find everything from quick snacks to full meals—and the layout makes it easy to settle in with friends or work on group projects. It also hosts plenty of events, so there’s always something happening that adds to the energy of the space. The tribute to John Lewis adds a meaningful touch, reminding everyone of his legacy of leadership and service. It really feels like a hub for campus life.
title: John Lewis Student Center

name: Quintin Kreth
text: The renovated student center opened in summer 2022. The new space has great light, but they bizarrely decided to decrease the already-limited dining options in the renovation. I have yet to get any remotely edible food from the 2nd-floor cafeteria. The Mexican place is particularly awful. The Chick-fil-A and Panda Express on the first floor are good, but this renovation wasted an opportunity to improve GT's longstanding weakness in dining options.

name: John Miller
text: The Student Center looks nice, but the so-called "New York" pizza at Ray's is disgusting.  The only reason you could possibly call it New York-style is due to its general shape.  My son had a cheese slice, and the cheese had neither the taste nor the consistency of mozzarella (or any cheese, for that matter).  I had a slice of Hawaiian.  It suffered from the same cheese, but they added pineapple and ham that was like eating small patches of leather.  One of the ham pieces was so tough that I honestly worried that there might be a piece of plastic melted on to it.  I saw that there was no line at Ray's, but a big line at the taco place.  I would suggest you try that place instead.  I left five stars for the Student Center, but the pizza is a zero!  Note: Service was good.  I hope the staff finds work at a better pizzeria.
